title: The Dogs Before the Map — Lawyer's Cave Coastal Alaska Femur, Koster & Stilwell II Intentional Dog Burials (~10,000 BP), Swan Point & Beringian Canids & Pre-Contact Indigenous American Dog Genomes

teenKit.tldr: A tiny, fingernail-sized bone fragment once mistaken for a bear turned out to be an ancient dog, completely rewriting our understanding of how and when dogs arrived in the Americas.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that ancient DNA trapped in microscopic scraps of bone can reveal migration stories that physical maps and visible artifacts completely miss.
keyTakeaways: A 1-centimeter femur fragment from Lawyer's Cave in Alaska completely changed timelines for early American dogs through paleogenomics.
Scientists must account for the radiocarbon reservoir effect, where a diet heavy in seafood makes ancient bones look artificially older than they actually are.
Ancient dog history isn't a smooth, continuous movie; instead, the archaeological record gives us disconnected snapshots that we must respect without over-mapping.

vocab.meaning: The study of animal remains, like bones and teeth, left behind by human activity in archaeological sites.
The recovery and analysis of ancient DNA from long-dead organisms to map out genetic history.
A dating distortion caused when animals eat marine foods that absorb older carbon from the ocean, making their bones test older than they are.
A member of the biological family that includes dogs, wolves, foxes, and coyotes.

quiz.question: What was the Lawyer's Cave femur fragment originally misidentified as?
quiz.explanation: Researchers sorted it as a bear bone because it was mixed with post-glacial bear remains and they were playing the statistical odds.

quiz.question: Why shouldn't scientists draw exact, connected migration routes on a map based on this data?
options: The maps are classified by the government
The genetic and radiocarbon models only provide isolated snapshots, not a continuous video
Dogs cannot walk across state lines
There are too many modern wolves in the way
quiz.explanation: The analytical boundaries of the data only support looking at distinct snapshots rather than a continuous, detailed travel diary.

quiz.question: How can a marine-heavy diet mess up radiocarbon dating?
options: It adds radioactive sugar to the DNA
It makes bones appear older than they really are due to older carbon in the ocean
It completely erases all genetic data
quiz.explanation: Marine environments contain older carbon reservoirs, which get absorbed into the food chain and throw off standard carbon-14 clocks.
